links_note: Site URL from her Clean Elections statement; not opened (outside this tool's provenance set).
party_note: No Labels Party of Arizona; coded 'I' in this module. Her Clean Elections statement says she is running as an Independent.

nominee.t: Won Arizona's first No Labels governor primary (Jul 21, 2026) by nearly 1,200 votes (about 12 points) over Hugh Lytle, the Scottsdale health-care CEO endorsed by party chair Paul Johnson, with fewer than 10,000 voters; Lytle conceded. Running mate: Angela Harrolle Mohan, a registered independent and former longtime CEO of The 100 Club (aid for families of public-safety personnel killed or seriously injured on duty).

ballot.t: On the general ballot under the No Labels label. KJZZ notes no third-party or independent governor candidate has topped 7% since 1986.

oneliner.t: Phoenix licensed professional counselor and small-business owner who, with about $40,000, upset the party-backed, largely self-funded candidate for the No Labels governor nomination.

born.t: Arizona (her statement: 'Arizona native'; date and place not found)

upbringing.t: By her own account she is an Arizona native, a mother and a small-business owner, a licensed professional counselor since 2017 with a PhD earned in 2018. She told KJZZ she was a lifelong Democrat, largely because of her parents, then registered Republican more recently ('I ran for 30 days, and it did not fit me') before running as No Labels. She describes her campaign as about 'people and a whole lot of Jesus and grit.' No independent biographical record was found.

career.role: Licensed professional counselor; mental-health practice owner (her account)

platform.t: Universal child care phased in on New Mexico's model; address child-care waitlists and benefit cliffs in rural counties such as Apache and Navajo.
Statewide conservation standards, local desalination, expanded municipal water connections in rural areas, well safety; Nevada as a conservation model; less long-term litigation.
Day-one temporary moratorium on new data-center applications; existing operations and jobs continue.
Opposes using federal health funds for broad tax cuts; warns cuts would hurt mental-health, addiction and disability services.
Keep the expanded ESA voucher program while improving public schools.
Homelessness, courts, rural communities, border control and legal immigration.

promises.t: Will not accept PAC or corporate donations.
Impose a temporary moratorium on new data-center applications on her first day.

claims.claim: Biggs has passed only one bill despite sponsoring thousands.

record.t: Official counts were not retrieved from congress.gov. A third-party aggregator lists about 896 sponsored measures (115th–119th Congresses), which suggests 'thousands' overstates; enacted count not established. Biggs replied that sponsorship rules explain why other members' names appear on bills he advanced (AMBER Alert in Indian Country, JACK Act, Right to Try).

claims.claim: Taxpayers have paid nearly $2 million toward Biggs's compensation over his career.

record.t: House salary records were not retrieved; the period counted (Congress only, or also state service) is unclear.

claims.claim: Arizona has about 46,246 No Labels voters and nearly 1.5 million independents, together nearly 36% of the electorate.
